description: This case study uses agent-based modelling to weigh the costs and benefits of managing demolition waste in Shenzhen, China, a city leading in this field. Zhikun Ding, Xiaoyan Cao, Yifei Wang, Huanyu Wu, Jian Zuo and George Zillante of Shenzhen University and the University of Adelaide published it in Waste Management in 2021. The model represents the interactions and adaptive behaviour of stakeholders such as demolition contractors and government, to show how economic instruments can push contractors towards low-impact waste management. The article is available online by subscription, and the abstract is free on PubMed. Coverage is the demolition of buildings in the city. Caveats: agent rules and cost parameters are not published with the abstract, and results are large aggregate figures for the study case. If traditional demolition stays the main choice, the net benefit of demolishing buildings in the case reaches minus 131.4 billion yuan, with costs above revenue; if contractors widely adopt selective demolition, the net benefit reaches 33.3 billion yuan, 125.34 percent better. The authors propose a management framework for stakeholders. Simulation uses: contractor behaviour and cost-benefit outcomes for construction and demolition waste policy models. Related records: the European construction and demolition waste recovery assessment (data-cdw-europe-analysis-code-and-data-for-a-european-assessment-of-construction-and-demolition-waste-recovery-p02965) gives open data on the same waste stream.
